correctness.rationale: Every Heawood perfect matching is exactly one admissible permutation of seven line labels. Flipping an alternating six-cycle is equivalent to changing exactly three permutation coordinates because two perfect matchings have symmetric difference a union of even cycles and a change on three points is one six-cycle. Exhaustive enumeration of all 5040 permutations yields 24 matchings and 84 flip edges. Every ordered vertex pair has the verified distance-intersection counts giving {7,4,1;1,2,7}. The explicit 24-image permutation compares all 576 entries with the published 24-Klein adjacency matrix. A separately structured checker generates all 28 six-cycles, changes matchings by edge symmetric difference, and agrees on every indexed edge (matching SHA-256 fingerprint d24c03e5de28643a1ab7271df299b66de1fc6d3e71d1ad151bfa2ce71911f04a). All eight one-factorizations and antipodal classes are checked in the same complete finite universe. Exact source programs and actual recorded outputs are included.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the explicit isomorphism from the Heawood matching hexagon-flip graph to the 24-vertex Klein graph. Dejter 2010 constructs the Klein graph via Coxeter graph seven-cycles and mentions Heawood six-cycles, but not perfect-matching flips. The known 24 Heawood matchings/eight factorizations and published 24-Klein adjacency table do not by themselves imply an adjacency-preserving bijection. No retrieved specific theorem covers the isomorphism, and targeted records searches found no equivalence. Priority risk from unindexed/inaccessible sources remains.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the whole natural local-move space of perfect matchings of the Heawood graph with an independently distinguished, highly symmetric graph from the Klein quartic map. It translates antipodal classes into the graph’s eight one-factorizations, determines optimal move distances and exact one-step branching, and provides an explicit structural equivalence absent from separate known counting tables. The motivation derives from canonical objects and a natural shortest alternating-cycle flip, not a fabricated slice of numerical invariants.
